sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.read_scope: Infobox only, for the publisher discrepancy.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 在《Impro》里把高地位和低地位各写成一句潜台词：演高地位的人是在说「别靠近我，我咬人」，演低地位的人是在说「别咬我，我不值得你费劲」。
claims.locator: Impro, Status chapter, p.43 (Routledge 2012 reprint; full-page preview)
claims.quote_en: A person who plays high status is saying 'Don't come near me, I bite.' Someone who plays low status is saying 'Don't bite me, I'm not worth the trouble.'
claims.limits: Popular quote lists reword this (Buteau: 'Don't touch me' / 'Don't hurt me'); use the book wording.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 自己把「人有偏好的地位，并会设法挪向偏好的位置」这个论断标成当下的看法：开头写的是 My belief (at this moment)。
claims.locator: Impro, p.43, paragraph beginning 'My belief (at this moment)'
claims.quote_en: My belief (at this moment) is that people have a preferred status; that they like to be low, or high, and that they try to manoeuvre themselves into the preferred positions.
claims.limits: The hedge is Johnstone's, in a 1979 book; later editions of the text are not compared.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 说，所演的地位是一种有效的防御，人会越来越被这种防御定型，成为只擅长一种地位的「status specialist」，被要求演相反地位时会觉得没有防护。
claims.locator: Impro, p.43, same paragraph block as the 'I bite' lines
claims.quote_en: You become a status specialist, very good at playing one status, but not very happy or competent at playing the other.
claims.limits: 'Asked to play the 'wrong' status, you'll feel 'un-defended'' is the next sentence; not quoted here.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 教学时先让学生体验各种地位感觉，之后才讨论含义甚至引入「status」这个词，用这种次序减少学生对地位概念的抵触。
claims.locator: Impro, p.42, paragraph beginning 'I minimise 'status resistance''
claims.quote_en: I minimise 'status resistance' from my students by getting them to experience various status sensations before I discuss the implications, or even introduce the term.
claims.limits: Describes his classroom practice, not a test of whether it works.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 在课上做了一个演示：说话时保持头部不动，然后告诉学生这会明显改变自己对自己的感受和别人对他的感受。
claims.locator: Impro, p.43, paragraph beginning 'Again I change my behaviour and become authoritative'
claims.quote_en: Finally I explain that I'm keeping my head still whenever I speak, and that this produces great changes in the way I perceive myself and am perceived by others.
claims.limits: Johnstone's own report of his own demonstration; no measurement. Confirms the head-still example Qureshi paraphrases.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 写到需要权威的角色（悲剧英雄之类）要学会头部不动：演掘墓人可以边说边晃头，演哈姆雷特不行。
claims.locator: Impro, p.43, same paragraph
claims.quote_en: Actors needing authority—tragic heroes and so on—have to learn this still head trick. You can talk and waggle your head about if you play the gravedigger, but not if you play Hamlet.
claims.limits: Closest text to Qureshi's 'moving your head side to side is low status'; Johnstone ties head movement to roles on stage, not to a general low-status rule.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 称，他说话时若保持头部不动，就会自动做出许多别的高地位行为：说完整的句子、保持眼神接触、动作更流畅、占更多「空间」。
claims.locator: Impro, p.44 (full-page preview), paragraph beginning 'These are just tricks'
claims.quote_en: If I speak with a still head, then I'll do many other high-status things quite automatically. I'll speak in complete sentences, I'll hold eye contact.
claims.limits: The same paragraph pairs toes pointing inward with a hesitant 'er' and covering the bottom lip; a one-person report, not a study.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 规定练习中学生的地位只能比搭档高一点或低一点，这样学生必须真正看着搭档，并按对方的行为来调整自己的行为。
claims.locator: Impro, p.44, paragraph beginning 'I insist that they have to get their status'
claims.quote_en: I insist that they have to get their status just a little above or below their partner's. This ensures that they really 'see' their partner
claims.limits: The preceding sentence lists the four exercise states: both lower, both raise, one raises while the other lowers, status reversed during the scene.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 说，地位练习一旦让地位技能变成自动反应，它们就会「锁定」对手演员，学生随即变得善于观察，看上去像经验丰富的即兴演员。
claims.locator: Impro, p.44, same paragraph
claims.quote_en: The automatic status skills then 'lock on to' the other actor, and the students are transformed into observant, and apparently very experienced improvisers.
claims.limits: Teacher's description of classroom results.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 认为这些地位练习在舞台上重现了现实生活的效果：每个人每时每刻都在把自己的地位向上或向下调整一点点。
claims.locator: Impro, p.44, same paragraph
claims.quote_en: These status exercises reproduce on the stage exactly the effects of real life, in which moment by moment each person adjusts his status up or down a fraction.
claims.limits: A claim about real life asserted from teaching experience; no cited study.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 自己承认，不同报告对眼神接触与支配的结论互相矛盾，他据此说明实际察觉地位交易是困难的。
claims.locator: Impro, p.42, paragraph beginning 'One might contrast this with other reports' (Stanford traffic-light experiment)
claims.quote_en: Such disagreements indicate the difficulty of actually perceiving status transactions.
claims.limits: A limit stated by the author; the preceding text contrasts an inventory finding with a Stanford experiment.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 把地位练习称为「拐杖」：它们托住演员，使本能系统得以运转，演员因此觉得一切很容易，也不觉得自己在「表演」。
claims.locator: Impro, p.46 (full-page preview), paragraph beginning 'I increase the confidence of the actors'
claims.quote_en: The status exercises are really crutches to support the actor so that instinctual systems can operate.
claims.limits: Same paragraph gives the breakfast / office / supper sequence in which husband and wife swap high and low.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 称，地位一旦像生活中那样变成自动反应，就能在完全没有准备的情况下即兴演出复杂的场景。
claims.locator: Impro, p.46, same paragraph
claims.quote_en: Once the status becomes automatic, as it is in life, it's possible to improvise complex scenes with no preparation at all.
claims.limits: Claim about his troupe's practice.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 写道，没有地位训练，他的即兴剧团 Theatre Machine 不可能在欧洲成功巡演，因为那样就得先排练场景。
claims.locator: Impro, p.46, paragraph beginning 'Without the status work'
claims.quote_en: Without the status work my improvisation group, the Theatre Machine, could never have toured successfully in Europe; not without preparing the scenes first.
claims.limits: Author's own account; no outside check.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 用一个「地狱」场景说明：被问到「Excrement」这类突如其来的台词时，知道自己演的是哪种地位，答案就会自动出来，不需要「想」。
claims.locator: Impro, p.46, 'Ah, another sinner!' example
claims.quote_en: If you know what status you're playing the answers come automatically.
claims.limits: The scene continues on p.46 (high: cold voice; low: 'Which ever you think best, Sir'); only the principle sentence is quoted.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 的「Smith 与 Sir」解雇场景里，如果 Smith 演高地位，说出「Won't you reconsider」就给了他一个巨大的对抗阻力，Sir 说再见时场面因此扣人心弦。
claims.locator: Impro, p.50 (full-page preview), commentary after the Smith / Sir dialogue
claims.quote_en: If Smith plays high, then saying 'Won't you reconsider' gives him an enormous resistance to work against.
claims.limits: Text before the dialogue (p.49) is not in the preview.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 称地位不仅演给人，也演给物：进入空的候诊室时可以对家具演高或低的地位，他还让等着搭档上场的演员「对长椅演低地位」。
claims.locator: Impro, p.50, paragraphs 'Status is played to anything' and 'An actor is waiting on stage'
claims.quote_en: Status is played to anything, objects as well as people.
claims.limits: The bench / pigeon example follows on the same page ('Play low status to the bench').

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 指出教地位互动时，学生有意识上愿意，潜意识里可能有很强的抵触，所以必须让学生觉得安全并对教师有信心。
claims.locator: Impro, p.55 (full-page preview), section '5 Status Specialists', first paragraph
claims.quote_en: however willing the student is consciously, there may be very strong subconscious resistances. Making the student safe, and getting him to have confidence in you, are essential.
claims.limits: Quote begins mid-sentence ('If you wish to teach status interactions, it's necessary to understand that ...').

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 在讲「status specialist」时写道：糟糕的戏剧学校会按类型选角，让人一直演自己偏好的地位，只利用已有的本事，不拓宽范围。这是他书中 cast 一词与地位相连的地方。
claims.locator: Impro, pp.55-56 (full-page preview; sentence runs across the page break)
claims.quote_en: In a bad drama school it's possible to play your 'preferred' status all the time, since they cast you to type, exploiting what you can do, instead of widening your range.
claims.limits: Drama-school casting sense. Search-inside for 'casting' finds only 'casting aside' (p.161); the book does not define 'casting' as a Palantir-style term.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 认为职业剧场里的演员大致分成高地位专才和低地位专才，并主张合格的演员训练应当教会所有类型的地位交易。
claims.locator: Impro, p.56 (full-page preview), first paragraph
claims.quote_en: A proper training for actors would teach all types of transaction.
claims.limits: Preceding sentences: actors divide roughly into high-status and low-status specialists.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 在 Status 一章开头写道，地位交易在现实中一直持续，不只发生在冲突时；他用公园里鸭子冲突之外也小心保持距离作类比。
claims.locator: Impro, p.33, chapter opening after the section title 'The See-saw' (snippet only)
claims.quote_en: In reality status transactions continue all the time.
claims.limits: Snippet view; surrounding text unread. The same page opens with the Royal Court Theatre Studio (1963) observation that actors 'couldn't reproduce ordinary conversation'.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 对「朋友之间不玩地位」这一反驳的回答是：熟人变成朋友，是因为双方同意一起玩地位游戏。
claims.locator: Impro, p.37 (snippet only)
claims.quote_en: My answer is that acquaintances become friends when they agree to play status games together.
claims.limits: Snippet; the explanation that follows is unread.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 设想，如果教师把地位交易当作游戏来教，团体的气氛会变好，一个竞争型的团体可能转为合作型。
claims.locator: Impro, p.35 (snippet only, two hits stitched: 'If he taught them to play status transactions as games ...' and 'the group might have flipped over ...')
claims.quote_en: the group might have flipped over from acting as a competitive group into acting as a co-operative one
claims.limits: Counterfactual about an unidentified 'he' in the surrounding text (likely a teacher; context unread). Do not present as a finding.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 把地位定义为一种做出来的行为，而不是社会身份：社会地位低的人可以演高地位，反之亦然，他随后用流浪汉与公爵夫人的对话举例。
claims.locator: Impro, p.36 (snippet only; the sentence begins 'Status is a confusing term unless it's ...' in another snippet)
claims.quote_en: something one does. You may be low in social status, but play high, and vice versa.
claims.limits: Quote starts mid-sentence; the lead-in words are not visible in the snippet that carries this text.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 写道，喜剧演员是被人付钱来降低自己或别人地位的人。
claims.locator: Impro, p.39 (snippet only)
claims.quote_en: A comedian is someone paid to lower his own or other people's status.
claims.limits: Snippet; the Ken Dodd example that follows is unread.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 称地位交易不只对即兴演员有意义：一旦懂得每个声音和姿势都暗示一种地位，人看世界的方式会变，而且这种改变大概是永久的。
claims.locator: Impro, p.72 (snippet only; end of Status chapter, which runs pp.33-74)
claims.quote_en: Once you understand that every sound and posture implies a status, then you perceive the world quite differently, and the change is probably permanent.
claims.limits: Snippet; author's claim from teaching experience.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 教学时先承担失败的责任，再要求学生用能学得最快的方式安排自己；他在书里说自己教的是 spontaneity。
claims.locator: Impro, p.32 (snippet only; 'Notes on Myself' chapter, pp.13-32)
claims.quote_en: In exchange for accepting the blame for failure, I ask the students to set themselves up in such a way that they'll learn as quickly as possible.
claims.limits: Snippet; ties to the Globe obituary recollection of him taking responsibility for students' scenes.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 把人分成偏好说 Yes 与偏好说 No 的两类，写道说 No 的人多得多，但可以训练一类人表现得像另一类；这句话前半（Yes 换来冒险，No 换来安全）与 2016 年 TEDx 的标题卡相同。
claims.locator: Impro, p.92 (snippet only), just before the 'Your name Smith?' exercise; first half in a second snippet: 'adventures they have, and those who say No are rewarded by the safety they attain'
claims.quote_en: There are far more 'No' sayers around than 'Yes' sayers, but you can train one type to behave like the other.
claims.limits: Snippet. The TEDx link rests on Alberta Views' report of a title card; the TEDx text itself was not read.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 在「Blocking and Accepting」一节写道：阻挡是一种攻击。理由是他让两个学生互说「我爱你」时，学生几乎总是接受对方的想法。
claims.locator: Impro, p.94, section 'Blocking and Accepting' (snippet only)
claims.quote_en: Blocking is a form of aggression. I say this because if I set up a scene in which two students are to say 'I love you' to each other, they almost always accept each other's ideas.
claims.limits: Snippet; the sentence continues ('Many students do their first interesting, unforced ...') and the argument that follows is unread.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 观察到有些学生偏好让步（他称这些人是「迷人」的人），多数学生则偏好阻挡，而且往往没意识到自己在阻挡。
claims.locator: Impro, p.95 (snippet only)
claims.quote_en: Some students prefer to yield (these are 'charming' people) but most prefer to block
claims.limits: Snippet; the end of the sentence ('even though they may have no idea ...') is cut off.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 的做法是给两个演员设定程序：A 提出并接受，B 提出并阻挡，借此训练和观察 offer、block、accept 三种动作。
claims.locator: Impro, p.97 (snippet only)
claims.quote_en: You can programme two actors so that A offers and accepts, and B offers and blocks.
claims.limits: Snippet; the example dialogue (A: 'Hallo, are you a new member?') is cut off.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 在 1979 年的书里写，出色的即兴演员看上去像心灵感应、一切像事先安排好，原因是他们接受对方给出的所有 offer，而这是「正常」人不会做的事。
claims.locator: Impro, p.99 (snippet only)
claims.quote_en: everything looks prearranged. This is because they accept all offers made—which is something no 'normal' person would do. Also they may accept offers which weren't really intended.
claims.limits: Snippet starting mid-sentence ('... telepathic;'); compare the 2007 interview in which he calls the 'accept all offers' rule a 'perversion'.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 要求演员不要去想一个 offer，而要假定对方已经给出了一个。
claims.locator: Impro, p.99 (snippet only)
claims.quote_en: I tell my actors never to think up an offer, but instead to assume that one has already been made.
claims.limits: Snippet; the Groucho Marx example that follows is unread.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 称学会接受 offer 之后，意外就不能再打断表演；他举了斯坦尼斯拉夫斯基责备椅子塌了的演员没有继续演的例子。
claims.locator: Impro, p.100 (snippet only)
claims.quote_en: Once you learn to accept offers, then accidents can no longer interrupt the action.
claims.limits: Snippet; the Stanislavsky anecdote is cut off.

claims.statement_zh: Johnstone 用一个例子说明新手为何受挫：新手伸出手试探是否下雨，搭档却握住他的手说「幸会」，新手便生气。
claims.locator: Impro, p.101 (snippet only)
claims.quote_en: An inexperienced improviser gets annoyed because his partners misunderstand him. He holds out his hand to see if it's raining, and his partner shakes it and says 'Pleased to meet you.'
claims.limits: Snippet; Johnstone's resolution of the example is unread.

claims.statement_zh: 在《Impro》里，「Yes, But」是一个众所周知的 accept-and-block 游戏，出自 Viola Spolin；其孪生游戏「Yes, and」是 accept-and-offer 游戏。书里把它们当作练习游戏，而不是通用规则。
claims.locator: Impro, p.103 (snippet only)
claims.quote_en: This is a well known 'accept-and-block' game (described in Viola Spolin, Improvisation for the Theatre). (Its twin game 'Yes, and ...' is an 'accept-and-offer' game
claims.limits: Snippet cut off after 'game'; the 'rule' reading of Yes-and is not in this text.

mechanisms.name: 地位是一种防御性的站位
mechanisms.how_it_works: Johnstone 认为人有偏好的地位（高或低），并把演出的地位当作防御：高地位说「别靠近我，我咬人」，低地位说「别咬我，我不值得你费劲」。人会被自己有效的防御定型成「status specialist」，被迫演相反地位时觉得没有防护。他把这个看法标为「My belief (at this moment)」。
mechanisms.demonstrable_as: 两栏卡片：高地位台词与低地位台词并排，下面叠一行小字「My belief (at this moment)」。

mechanisms.name: 身体与声音的标记会成串联动
mechanisms.how_it_works: 说话时头不动，会连带出现完整句子、稳定眼神、更流畅的动作和更多空间；脚尖朝内则连带出现迟疑的 er、抿唇的笑和略喘的声音。短 er 是邀请别人打断，长 er 是「别打断我」。Johnstone 的教学次序是先让学生体验，再命名。
mechanisms.demonstrable_as: 两个火柴人对话：一个头不动、整句、直视；一个头晃动、带 er；用逐项出现的标签展示连带关系。

mechanisms.name: 比搭档只高一点或低一点，逼出观察
mechanisms.how_it_works: 练习规定双方地位只能比对方高或低一点点，演员必须真看搭档并据此调整自己；地位技能因此「锁定」对手，学生变得善于观察。Johnstone 说这等于在台上重现现实里每个人每时每刻微调地位的过程。
mechanisms.demonstrable_as: 两格四态图（同降、同升、一升一降、中途反转），用跷跷板表示相对位置。

mechanisms.name: 地位当拐杖，换来无需准备的反应速度
mechanisms.how_it_works: 地位一旦自动化，演员不用想就知道怎样接对方的话；Johnstone 称这是 Theatre Machine 不排练也能巡演的原因，也把地位练习叫作托住本能系统的拐杖。
mechanisms.demonstrable_as: 「Ah, another sinner!」场景：同一句台词，演高地位与低地位各自的回答对比。

mechanisms.name: 阻挡、让步与接受（offer-block-accept）
mechanisms.how_it_works: 把搭档的每个动作看成 offer，可被阻挡、让步或接受。Johnstone 说阻挡是攻击，多数学生偏好阻挡且常不自知；他让演员「假定一个 offer 已经给出」，并用程序化练习（A 提出并接受，B 提出并阻挡）训练。「Yes, and」在书里只是一个 accept-and-offer 练习。
mechanisms.demonstrable_as: 三条泳道的对话：伸手试雨，搭档说「幸会」，新手阻挡、让步、接受各演一遍。

mechanisms.name: 教师自己降低地位与不投票的协作姿态
mechanisms.how_it_works: Johnstone 的学生回忆他开课坐在地上、承担责任、随学期抬高自己的地位；他自己写下不投票（投票产生赢家输家），而是不断提出新想法直到对方说「好」。这些是他的做法的第一手与目击记录。
mechanisms.demonstrable_as: 一条随学期上升的地位曲线，旁边标出坐地、并排坐、共用笔记三个节点（均据 Globe 报道）。

visual_ideas: 跷跷板（原书第一节标题 The See-saw）：两人头部姿势不同，板子的倾斜随台词交替；p.44 的四种状态做成四格。
p.44 的连锁标签：头不动 → 整句话 → 眼神接触 → 动作流畅 → 占更多空间，逐项出现。
p.43 的 er：画两条时间线，短 er 之后别人插话，长 er 之后没人插话（据书中文字，不加数据）。
offer-block-accept 三泳道：「伸手试雨」这个例子，用同一句 offer 演三种回应。
对照幻灯片：1979 年书中「they accept all offers」与 2007 年访谈中「perversion」并排，标注年份和来源，不下结论。
Qureshi 说法的核对表：头不动（p.43 有）、哈姆雷特与掘墓人（p.43 有）、露手与插口袋（未找到）、casting（书中只有按类型选角的用法）。
排版引文页：用打字排版重现 p.43 的短引文，不使用页面截图。
limits_and_counterexamples: Johnstone 自己把地位论断标为暂时看法（My belief (at this moment)），并承认察觉地位交易很难，不同报告对眼神接触的结论互相矛盾（p.42）。
地位练习的前提是让学生觉得安全并对教师有信心；Johnstone 写到学生可能有很强的潜意识抵触（p.55）。把这套练习搬到客户现场不是书里的论断，只是 Qureshi 的推论。
Johnstone 2007 年在电话采访中把「接受所有 offer」这条规则称为 perversion（Georgia Straight）；而 1979 年的书里写出色即兴演员「接受所有 offer」（p.99）。两者的具体矛盾点不明，可能是对规则化的反对而不是对书中描述的反对，目前无法判定。
书里「Yes, and」只是 accept-and-offer 练习，与 Yes, But 成对（p.103，Spolin 一脉）；把它当作 Palantir 或即兴界的通用规则，在可读文本里没有依据。
Qureshi 的身体例子只部分能在书里核对：头不动成立；露手与插口袋没查到；casting 在书里只是学校按类型选角。他的段落是转述，不是 Johnstone 的原话。
Johnstone 的方法来自演员训练，他说自己教的是自发性（Impro p.32）。把它说成「拆解社会行为的机制」是 Qureshi 的概括；Johnstone 书中的材料是他教学观察的报告，没有对照实验。
网络上流传的《Impro》语录有改写（Buteau 清单），使用前必须对原书核对页码。
只有 pp.42-46、50、55-56 能读到整页；其余只有 2 到 3 行片段，因此论证中间的环节（例如 pp.47-49、51-54 的练习）读不到。
cannot_say: 不能说读过《Impro》的 Status 全章：只读到 pp.42-44、46、50、55-56 的整页，p.33-41、45、47-49、51-54、57-74 只有片段或没有；也不能转述 Spontaneity 章 pp.91-103 的完整论证，只有片段。
不能说 2018 年 Bloomsbury Revelations 版与 2012 年 Routledge 重印版页码相同；所有页码仅指后者。
不能说 Palantir 内部如何实际使用《Impro》：除 Qureshi 外没有找到第二位一手人证；其余网文都是评论者的推论。
不能说「casting」是《Impro》里的术语，或说明它在 Palantir 的含义；书里只有按类型选角的用法（pp.55-56）。
不能把「站直露手是高地位、驼背手插口袋是低地位」归给 Johnstone；书中可读页没有这一对。
不能逐字引用任何 Johnstone 教授地位的视频（Totino 的 Master-Servant 节选、Bev Fox 的 Status 片段、剧院博物馆第 18 段、TEDxYYC）：全部没有取得文字稿，只读到元数据。
不能说 Johnstone 赞成或反对「Yes, and」规则：2017 年剧院博物馆访谈第 18 段未读；2007 年访谈只有他把「accept all offers」称为 perversion 一句。
不能说 Johnstone 本人发布过免费的地位教学视频：官方站和 ITI 站只卖或登记 DVD，免费视频均为第三方上传。

density.reasons: 地位这一半有完整的一手可读弧线：问题（演员做不出普通对话，人人都在做地位交易，p.33 片段）、机制（偏好地位是防御，p.43；标记会成串联动，pp.43-44；比搭档只高低一点来锁定观察，p.44）、例子（头不动、er、Smith 与 Sir，pp.43-44、50）、限度（他自己的 My belief (at this moment)、察觉地位很难 p.42、需要安全 p.55、specialist 的局限 pp.55-56）。接受与阻挡一半只有片段，但片段足以立起问题到例子的链条（p.94 阻挡是攻击、p.95 多数人偏好阻挡、p.99 假定 offer 已给出、p.101 伸手试雨），再加 Johnstone 博客里的第一手协作做法、2007 年他对「accept all offers」的批评作限度。Palantir 一端只有 Qureshi 一人，必须标为他的说法。建议单独成集，范围收窄：以 Status 为主（用整页可读的 pp.42-46、50、55-56），accept/block 作第二拍，且只用片段级引文，不展开全章论证。若需要覆盖 Spontaneity 章的完整论证，须先取得合法的完整副本。

open_gaps: 取得合法的完整副本（购买或使用者已有），读 pp.33-41、47-49、51-54、57-74（Status 其余部分）与 pp.91-103（Blocking and Accepting 的完整论证），并核对 2018 Bloomsbury 版页码。
